# Set72 independent allocation reference source

This source is prepared before dependent product implementation. **It has not
been executed to generate expectations or size results.** Root must review and
freeze the exact inputs, final adopted contract and source set first. No script
creates its own approval lock, modifies an input or overwrites an output.

The staged catalog is `../reference-inputs/catalog.json`; its lock is
`../reference-inputs/input-lock.json`. The 33 inputs are byte-identical copies
of public qualified commit files, one explicitly historical proposal snapshot,
and a literal modeled-ID recipe. All wallet/account databases, private recovery
exports and private fixture fields are excluded. The source-only proposal input
is not an adopted contract: the execution lock separately pins the final
adopted contract supplied through `--contract`.

`public_derivation.py` uses CKDpub from the old public branch keys. The inherited
arithmetic module is loaded only after execution admission; no mnemonic/seed or
private derivation function is called. Every previously frozen native84 sparse
address is checked, and destination encoding/draft digests are compared with
all 24 old Set68 cases before new states are assembled. The binding IDs used in
this corpus remain synthetic IDs inherited from the previous independent model.

`allocation_model.py` models ordered bytes, reserve/consume/ack/burn, monotonic
head/metadata, host/local pairing, replay, capacity and exact local digests. Its
public derivation callable is an oracle math seam, **not** a proposed wallet API
or evidence callback. Injected invalid-child traces are separately labeled.
`case-plan.json` is the complete finite case inventory. There is one coherent
core corpus, including one full count boundary; no additional profile corpus.

## Separate sizing admission

`sizing.py` is a standalone stdlib-only diagnostic. It constructs conservative
width witnesses directly from old public initial manifests and the proposed
field order. It may run before final contract adoption only under an explicit
root lock with these fields:

```json
{"approved_by":"root","execution_authorized":true,"purpose":"set72-sizing","sources":{"sizing.py":"EXACT_SHA256"},"input_lock_sha256":"EXACT_SHA256"}
```

Invocation:

```text
python3 sizing.py --execute --approved-lock ROOT_LOCK --approved-lock-sha256 LOCK_SHA --input-lock ../reference-inputs/input-lock.json --inputs ../reference-inputs/inputs --output NEW_OUTPUT
```

It checks complete combined row/link/batch and guard/INIT/setup/READY sizes,
including file LF. It reports independent 4 MiB limits and logical 16 MiB work
accounting; it does not assert that every maximum-sized row fits simultaneously
or that this is a process heap bound. Maximum-width witnesses may deliberately
combine semantically incompatible values. They are not valid-state vectors.

## Core execution admission

The core lock must contain `approved_by: "root"`, `execution_authorized: true`,
`final_contract_reviewed: true`, `contract_sha256`, `input_lock_sha256`, and the
exact complete `sources` filename-to-SHA256 map declared by the generator.

```text
python3 generate_reference.py --execute --approved-producer-lock ROOT_LOCK --approved-lock-sha256 LOCK_SHA --input-lock ../reference-inputs/input-lock.json --inputs ../reference-inputs/inputs --contract ADOPTED_CONTRACT --output NEW_OUTPUT
```

The command verifies every source and catalog byte before and after work. It
rejects symlinked/escaping inputs and writes exclusively. Its stdout is a small
public size/hash/count report. Use a finite process bound (five minutes is a
ceiling for the complete public-derivation/count model), preserve failures and
reproduce with another qualified Python version before installing the corpus.
This does not use normal PoW or access a daemon.

No generated bytes prove account authority, concrete owner pointers, session
fences, atomic disk commits, background watches, cancellation/Close joins,
production custody or active replacement-wallet control. Those remain focused
implementation and actual fixture qualifications.
